J." Hampton Jr.''' (born February 7, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[New Zealand Breakers]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL). He was a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] at [[Little Elm High School]] in [[Little Elm, Texas]]. Hampton was recruited by top [[NCAA Division I]] programs but chose to bypass college and play one season professionally before the [[2020 NBA draft]]. ==High school career== Since his freshman season, Hampton played [[varsity team|varsity]] basketball for [[Little Elm High School]] in [[Little Elm, Texas]]. In his first high school game on November 17, 2016, he led all scorers with 33 points in a 78–52 win over [[Naaman Forest High School]].{{cite web |last1=Murphy |first1=Bryan |title=Time for hoops: Little Elm dismantles Naaman in season opener |url=https://starlocalmedia.com/friscoenterprise/sports/time-for-hoops-little-elm-dismantles-naaman-in-season-opener/article_549fe754-acef-11e6-9276-1f3615fd89f0.html |website=Frisco Enterprise |publisher=Star Local Media |accessdate=May 28, 2019 |date=November 17, 2016}} As a freshman, Hampton averaged 23.6 points, 7.2 rebounds, 4.2 assists, and 3.5 steals per game, leading Little Elm to a 29–5 record and the District 14-5A title.{{cite web |last1=Murphy |first1=Bryan |title=Home is where the heart is: Little Elm basketball star R.J. Hampton decides to stay with Lobos |url=https://starlocalmedia.com/friscoenterprise/sports/home-is-where-the-heart-is-little-elm-basketball-star/article_39d93da4-7bd3-11e7-90ec-dbcdaa01e2f8.html |website=Frisco Enterprise |publisher=Star Local Media |accessdate=May 28, 2019 |date=August 7, 2017}}{{cite web |last1=Wixon |first1=Matt |title=SportsDayHS 2017 All-Area boys basketball teams, newcomer and coach of the year |url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/high-school/high-schools/2017/03/23/sportsdayhs-2017-area-boys-basketball-teams-newcomer-coach-year |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |accessdate=May 28, 2019 |date=March 23, 2017}} He was named to the [[MaxPreps]] Freshman All-American first team and earned Texas Association of Basketball Coaches (TABC) Class 5A All-State and ''[[The Dallas Morning News|Dallas Morning News]]'' All-Area Newcomer of the Year honors.{{cite web |title=2016-17 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Freshman All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/EVB78NqOWEaYDifF0xyXpg/2016-17-maxpreps-boys-basketball-freshman-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |accessdate=May 28, 2019 |date=April 18, 2017}} In May 2017, Hampton announced that he was transferring to the nationally-ranked basketball program of [[Montverde Academy]] in [[Montverde, Florida]], before deciding to return to Little Elm.{{cite web |last1=Wixon |first1=Matt |title=R.J. Hampton, one of the nation's top basketball recruits, ditches Montverde Academy to stay at Little Elm |url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/high-school/high-schools/2017/08/04/star-guard-rj-hampton-one-nations-top-recruits-staying-little-elm-instead-transferring-montverde-academy |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |accessdate=May 28, 2019 |date=August 4, 2017}} In the 2017–18 season, Hampton averaged 30.3 points, 8.8 rebounds, six assists, 4.4 steals, and 2.5 blocks per game, guiding Little Elm to a 28–8 record.{{cite web |last1=Florek |first1=Michael |title=Meet the best boys basketball players in Dallas: The 2018 Dallas Morning News all-area team |url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/high-school/high-schools/2018/03/22/meet-best-boysbasketball-players-dallas-2018-dallas-morning-news-area-team |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |accessdate=May 28, 2019 |date=March 22, 2018}} He garnered MaxPreps Sophomore All-American first team, ''[[USA Today]]'' All-Texas first team, and TABC 5A All-State recognition.{{cite web |last1=Divens |first1=Jordan |title=2017-18 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Sophomore All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/yL1wLxRGiUeRCLlOOrsePA/2017-18-maxpreps-boys-basketball-sophomore-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |accessdate=May 28, 2019 |date=April 17, 2018}}{{cite web |title=2017-18 ALL-USA Texas Boys Basketball Team |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2018/2017-18-all-usa-texas-boys-basketball-team |website=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=May 28, 2019 |date=April 16, 2018}} On December 14, 2018, Hampton scored 33 points in an 80–66 victory over [[South Garland High School]], matching up against fellow coveted recruit [[Tyrese Maxey]].{{cite web |last1=Jennings |first1=Randy |title=R.J. Hampton, Little Elm top Tyrese Maxey, South Garland in showdown of Texas' top basketball prospects |url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/high-school/high-schools/2018/12/14/rj-hampton-little-elm-top-tyrese-maxey-south-garland-showdown-texas-top-basketball-prospects |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |accessdate=May 29, 2019 |date=December 14, 2018}} On December 29, he posted a career-high 50 points, 12 rebounds, seven assists, and six steals in an 86–62 win over [[Coppell High School]].{{cite web |last1=Jordan |first1=Jason |title=Chosen 25 PG R.J. Hampton scores career-high 50 points |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2018/chosen-25-pg-r-j-hampton-scores-career-high-50-points |website=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=May 29, 2019 |date=December 29, 2018}} In February 2019, Hampton had another 50-point game in an 83–80 loss to [[Northwest High School (Texas)|Northwest High School]].{{cite web |last1=Murphy |first1=Bryan |title=Column: Hampton robbed of District MVP |url=https://starlocalmedia.com/friscoenterprise/sports/column-hampton-robbed-of-district-mvp/article_0cbaa4ec-41c6-11e9-bbe4-573fb4339118.html |website=Frisco Enterprise |publisher=Star Local Media |accessdate=May 29, 2019 |date=March 8, 2019}} As a junior, Hampton averaged 32 points, 9.7 rebounds, 6.4 assists, and 3.9 steals per game, helping Little Elm achieve a 24–10 record.{{cite web |title=R.J. Hampton 2018 - 2019 Texas Boys Basketball Player of the Year |url=https://playeroftheyear.gatorade.com/winner/rj-hampton/37167 |publisher=[[Gatorade]] |accessdate=May 29, 2019}} On March 15, he was named Texas [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]], becoming the first non-senior to win the award since [[Justise Winslow]] in 2013.{{cite web |last1=Hoyt |first1=Joseph |title=Little Elm star R.J. Hampton named Gatorade's Texas basketball Player of the Year and finalist for national award |url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/high-school/high-schools/2019/03/15/little-elm-star-rj-hampton-named-gatorades-texas-basketball-player-year-finalist-national-award |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |accessdate=April 30, 2019 |date=March 15, 2019}} He also earned ''USA Today'' All-USA first team and MaxPreps All-American second team distinction.{{cite web |title=2018-19 ALL-USA High School Boys Basketball: First Team |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2019/2018-19-all-usa-high-school-boys-basketball-first-team#slideIdslide-2 |publisher=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=April 30, 2019 |date=April 2, 2019}}{{cite web |last1=Divens |first1=Jordan |title=MaxPreps 2018-19 High School Boys Basketball All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/mdbwDYCSa02E7-TpRc5Gmg/maxpreps-2018-19-high-school-boys-basketball-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |accessdate=April 30, 2019 |date=April 11, 2019}} On April 30, Hampton reclassified to the 2019 class, forgoing his senior year and graduating from high school after about three weeks of online classes.{{cite web |last1=Hill |first1=Drew |title=Five-star Memphis basketball target R.J. Hampton reclassifies to 2019 |url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/college/memphis-tigers/basketball/2019/04/30/memphis-basketball-tigers-target-r-j-hampton-reclassifies-2019/3628389002/ |website=[[The Commercial Appeal]] |accessdate=April 30, 2019 |date=April 30, 2019}} ===Recruiting=== Hampton was a consensus five-star recruit and ranked among the top six players in the 2019 recruiting class.{{cite web |title=R.J. Hampton, 2019 Point guard |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2019/r-j-hampton-182969 |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |accessdate=May 29, 2019}}{{cite web |title=RJ Hampton, Little Elm, Combo Guard |url=https://247sports.com/Player/RJ-Hampton-46036336/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |accessdate=May 29, 2019}}{{cite web |title=R.J. Hampton |url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/230214/rj-hampton |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=May 29, 2019}} On September 5, 2017, Christian Dawkins, an agent later indicted in the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball corruption scandal|NCAA basketball corruption scandal]], expressed a desire to pay Hampton in emails sent to business partners. When the emails surfaced in 2019, Hampton's father denied ever meeting Dawkins.{{cite web |last1=Schlabach |first1=Mark |title=Christian Dawkins' emails detail payment plans to several players |url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/25210341/ncaa-gets-approval-investigate-schools-college-basketball-corruption-case |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=May 29, 2019 |date=January 3, 2019}} Before reclassifying on April 30, 2019, Hampton had been considered one of the best prospects in the 2020 class.{{cite web |last1=Newman |first1=Logan |title=Report: R.J. Hampton cuts list to four schools, could reclassify to 2019 |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2019/rj-hampton-top-four-duke-kansas-kentucky-memphis-report |website=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=May 29, 2019 |date=April 7, 2019}} He narrowed down his potential college destinations to [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]], and [[Texas Tech Red Raiders men's basketball|Texas Tech]].{{cite web |last1=Boone |first1=Kyle |title=Five-star guard RJ Hampton to play in Australian NBL, rejects Kansas, Memphis, Texas Tech |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/college-basketball-recruiting-five-star-guard-rj-hampton-to-play-in-australian-nbl-rejects-kansas-memphis-texas-tech/ |publisher=[[CBS Sports]] |accessdate=May 29, 2019 |date=May 28, 2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = R. J. Hampton | position = [[Point guard|PG]] | hometown = [[Little Elm, Texas|Little Elm, TX]] | highschool = [[Little Elm High School|Little Elm]] (TX) | feet = 6 | inches = 5 | weight = 180 | 40 = | commitdate = — | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 96 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2019 | rivals ref title = | scout ref title = | espn ref title = | rivals school = | scout s = | espn schoolid = | 247 overall = 5 | rivals overall = 6 | espn overall = 5 | accessdate = April 30, 2019 | bball = yes }} ==Professional career== ===New Zealand Breakers (2019–2020)=== On May 28, 2019, Hampton signed a multi-year deal with the [[New Zealand Breakers]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL), which is based in Australia, with the option to leave for the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).{{cite web |last1=Slagter |first1=Josh |title=RJ Hampton, a top-5 national recruit, chooses to play pro basketball in New Zealand: 'You can always go back to college' |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-spt-rj-hampton-new-zealand-pro-basketball-college-20190528-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |accessdate=May 29, 2019 |date=May 28, 2019}} He said that he skipped college basketball because he wanted to "live like a pro and to play with grown men and not have to juggle books and basketball."{{cite web |title=Top US prospect R.J. Hampton signs with New Zealand team |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/nba/top-us-prospect-rj-hampton-signs-with-new-zealand-team/2019/05/29/503db8f4-81d0-11e9-b585-e36b16a531aa_story.htoml |website=[[The Washington Post]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=May 29, 2019 |date=May 29, 2019}} Hampton joined the Breakers through the NBL Next Stars program, which aims to develop [[NBA draft]] prospects.{{cite web |title=US Teen Sensation Signs with NZ Breakers |url=https://www.nzbreakers.basketball/news/article/us-teen-sensation-signs-with-nz-breakers |publisher=[[New Zealand Breakers]] |accessdate=May 29, 2019 |date=May 28, 2019}}{{cite web |title=NBL to Fast Track Next Stars of the NBA |url=http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/nbl-to-fast-track-next-stars-of-the-nba |publisher=[[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] |accessdate=May 29, 2019 |date=March 2, 2018}} On September 20, he made his professional debut in a win over [[Melbourne United]], recording 11 points, three rebounds and four assists in 21 minutes.{{cite web |last1=Taylor |first1=Cody |title=R.J. Hampton drops 11 points in NBL debut with the NZ Breakers |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2019/09/20/r-j-hampton-nbl-new-zealand-breakers-debut-preseason-stats-highlights/ |website=The Rookie Wire |accessdate=December 20, 2019 |date=September 20, 2019}} Two days later, he posted a season-high 20 points, five rebounds and three steals in a loss to the [[South East Melbourne Phoenix]].{{cite web |title=RJ Hampton shines, top scores as Breakers fall in second pre-season clash |url=https://www.tvnz.co.nz/one-news/sport/basketball/rj-hampton-shines-top-scores-breakers-fall-in-second-pre-season-clash |website=[[TVNZ]] |accessdate=January 18, 2020 |date=September 21, 2019}} On November 9, Hampton was ejected four minutes into a game against South East Melbourne after attempting to put his arm around the neck of opposing guard [[John Roberson]] during a scuffle.{{cite web |last1=Robinson |first1=Jesse |title=RJ Hampton ejected early in NBL tussle |url=https://www.espn.com/nbl/story/_/id/28039053/rj-hampton-ejected-nbl-tussle |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=December 20, 2019 |date=November 9, 2019}} On December 11, it was announced that he would miss about four weeks of action with a hip injury.{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Projected NBA lottery pick RJ Hampton to miss 4 weeks with hip injury |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28278222/projected-nba-lottery-pick-rj-hampton-miss-4-weeks-hip-injury |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=December 20, 2019 |date=December 11, 2019}} On January 5, 2020, Hampton returned, scoring 11 points in a win over South East Melbourne.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28415031/sources-rj-hampton-cleared-practice-lamelo-ball-remains-sidelined|title=Sources: Hampton cleared; LaMelo remains out|date=2020-01-03|website=ESPN.com|language=en|access-date=2020-01-03}} He parted ways with the Breakers on February 4 to return to the United States and prepare for the [[2020 NBA draft]]. Through 15 NBL games, Hampton averaged 8.8 points, 3.9 rebounds and 2.4 assists per game, shooting 40.7 percent from the field.{{cite web |last1=Reive |first1=Christopher |title=RJ Hampton leaves New Zealand Breakers to prepare for NBA draft |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/news/article.cfm?c_id=4&objectid=12305812 |website=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |accessdate=February 3, 2020 |date=February 3, 2020}} ==National team career== Hampton won the gold medal at the [[2017 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship]] with the [[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|United States national under-16 team]]. In five games, he averaged nine points, 3.2 rebounds and 2.6 assists per game.{{cite web |last1=Zagoria |first1=Adam |title=R.J. Hampton looking to win second straight gold medal with USA Basketball, plans to cut college list during winter |url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2018/06/21/rj-hampton-looking-to-win-second-straight-gold-medal-with-usa-basketball-plans-to-cut-college-list-during-winter/ |publisher=ZagsBlog |accessdate=April 30, 2019 |date=June 21, 2018}} He won another gold medal with the national under-17 team at the [[2018 FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup]] but was limited to two games by a foot injury. Hampton averaged 7.5 points, 2.5 rebounds and 1.5 steals per game.{{cite web |last1=Riddle |first1=Greg |title=Denton Guyer's De'Vion Harmon and Little Elm's R.J. Hampton help USA win FIBA under-17 World Cup in Argentina |url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/high-school/high-schools/2018/07/08/denton-guyers-devion-harmon-little-elms-rj-hampton-helpusa-win-fiba-17-world-cup-argentina |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |accessdate=April 30, 2019 |date=July 8, 2018}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBL=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 NBL season|2019–20]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 New Zealand Breakers season|New Zealand]] | 15 || 12 || 20.6 || .407 || .295 || .679 || 3.9 || 2.4 || 1.1 || .3 || 8.8 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Hampton's father Rod Hampton played [[college basketball]] for [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball|SMU]] from 1987 to 1991.{{cite web |last1=Murphy |first1=Bryan |title=Leading the pack: No sophomore slump for superstar RJ Hampton |url=https://starlocalmedia.com/littleelmjournal/leading-the-pack-no-sophomore-slump-for-superstar-rj-hampton/article_74cdf39a-fbb3-11e7-a5b7-cb956036627f.html |website=Little Elm Journal |accessdate=April 30, 2019 |date=January 17, 2018}} His grandfather Richard Evans served in the [[Vietnam War]].{{cite web |title=R.J.
